correctness.rationale: Read the entire displayed coefficient C(K), k and L(K) in arXiv:2609.33140v1 Theorem 1.5. With c=cosh((log K)/2), s=sinh((log K)/2), k=s/c, L=2c/(1+c), the product (kL/2)*s=(s²)/(1+c)=c-1 exactly. Hence C(K)=C0 c+(c-1)(3sqrt3/2+coth(2c/(1+c))). Derivative in c is C0+A+coth(ell)-2(c-1)/(c+1)^2*csch²(ell)>C0+A+3/4>0 because ell>=1 and 2(c-1)/(c+1)^2<=1/4. c=1+q²/8+O(q4) gives exact alpha=(C0+A+coth1)/8=0.69887946077..., no odd term. No claim of fixed-K optimality follows.
